#summary This are guidelines on how to design a model that is to be used with EMFStore

= Obligatory Rules: Do´s and Dont´s =

   * All model elements *must* have "ModelElement" set as superclass in the Ecore. Please note that this restriction will be removed with EMFStore 0.7.
   * The id property *must NOT* be set for any model element feature
   * The property "resolveProxies" of References *must* be left at its default value "true". Please note that if you generate your Ecore from XML-Schemata the value might be set to false. Reset it to true in this case. 
   * In the genmodel the property "containmentproxies" must be set to "true"
   * Do *NOT* use simple attributes with a multiplicity greater than 1.
   * Do *NOT* set unsetable to true for any feature
   * Do *NOT* create non-transient references to anything other than model element subtypes. Non-transient references are allowed since they will not be saved.
   * Do *NOT* use the URI "/plugin/org.eclipse.emf.ecore/model/Ecore.ecore#//". Use the "http://..." URIs
   * Do *NOT* use generics in the Ecore!
   * Do *NOT* just override a getter or setter! If you want to override a setter or getter follow the recommended best practice in emf:
      * Rename generated setter or getter to get/setXGen
      * Write your own getter/setter marked with @generated NOT and call the get/setXGen
      * Your added code must be null safe for any input parameter!
      * Emf will now always update the generated part but leave your code untouched 

= Optional Rules =
   * All reference features of model elements *should* have the key property set to "identifier". This makes the stored models more robust against failures.
